_why: ADR 0063 says the substrate publishes base images and the application composes base plus overlay. Nothing published them, and two CI comments said mind-pod-rails-base 'does not exist and never will' as a pullable name. This declares which images this substrate publishes, so a consumer has something to pin and a gate can hold the set both ways.

tagging.rule: immutable tag per commit: sha-<full 40-char commit SHA>
tagging.no_latest: A mutable tag is not a pin. This repo already refuses undigested FROM lines (check_base_digests.py); publishing a moving :latest and inviting consumers to build FROM it would give back what that gate buys.
tagging.consumer_guidance: Resolve the digest and pin that: docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/laquereric/magentic-stack/rails-base:sha-<SHA>

published.name: rails-base
published.because: The platform base. Its own header says consumers build a thin image FROM it. app-oriented-translation's Dockerfile.thin is exactly that consumer.

published.name: switch
published.because: The LLM plane. An application composing the pod runs it unchanged; it has no application-specific content.

published.name: mind
published.because: MIND. Needs the nooa submodule checked out (compose named context nooa_src); an application cannot build it from a plain clone -- the strongest single reason to publish rather than have every consumer reproduce this.
published._build_contexts_why: mind/Dockerfile COPYs from two NAMED contexts and publish-images passed neither, so buildx read 'nooa_src' as a Docker Hub image and failed with 'pull access denied ... docker.io/library/nooa_src'. nooa_src is the PARENT of the pin because NOOA's own .dockerignore excludes *.md while its pyproject force-includes THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; .dockerignore is context-root scoped, so naming the parent sidesteps it without forking a FOLLOW-THEM tree. Declared here so the workflow carries no path literal.

published.name: front-base
published.because: Bun FRONT base (ADR 0072). Skeleton, 19 widget modules, Core homepage stub, A2UI KIND_MAP copy. Overlays FROM this digest. FLOOR-FRONT.json is a human pin; do not auto-bump.

not_published.because: The substrate's OWN Rails app (BACK and its roles). An application overlay builds its own thin layer FROM rails-base instead of consuming this one.

mind-pod FRONT overlay on front-base. Core is the homepage; the notes page and its routes are overlay files, not a second FRONT family. It publishes nothing: the overlay ships as mind-pod-front, the pod's seventh image lineage, built FROM the already-published front-base rather than published itself. The base pin is front-base:local; FLOOR-FRONT.json was re-measured by hand at 32b1d6d.
The CPCP FRONT accessory, paired to a specific BACK deployment. Not a substrate primitive.
Adapter wrapping the pinned upstream; built as part of switch, not shipped separately.

A DEVELOPER TOOL, not a substrate primitive. bin/ci-local builds it locally to run the CI gate on Linux over a clean clone before pushing; nothing in the pod runs it and no overlay builds FROM it. Publishing it would invite consumers to depend on a test harness.

_platforms_why: AMD64 AND ARM64, BECAUSE A FLOOR WITH ONE ARCHITECTURE IS TWO FLOORS. This was amd64-only, and said so honestly -- the workflow originally named no platform at all and built whatever the runner was, which was true by accident rather than by decision until 2026-09-04 made it a declaration. But the consequence outlived the fix: FLOOR.json had to carry a LOCAL arm64 digest with index_digest false for developers AND a separate, older GHCR amd64 index for deployment, and an overlay built against the first fails on the second with 'no match for platform in manifest list' -- which reads like a bad pin and is not one. The stewardship-intelligence overlay analysis named that split as its blocking gap (SI-G7) once the actor work closed the previous one. linux/arm64 is emulated on this runner and is the slow half; that is the price of one pullable floor identity instead of two unpullable ones. check_published_images holds this against the workflow, so adding or removing an architecture means changing both and neither can drift silently.
_scan_note: Directory names skipped when enumerating Dockerfiles. Held here as DATA, not as a literal in the checker. The trees they name are gitignored: present in a working clone, absent in a clean checkout. Enumerating them would give the gate two populations and a CI-only failure.
